# 1.2.76 - a room tile under the clock, and Foundry's sidebar and scene controls in two windows

One stage on the way to 1.3.0 (E77, the owner's request A8), released alone: every player, and a GM with a Monokuma, sees the room
their character stands in on a tile under the clock, with the GM's picture and description; the clock loses its room lines;
Foundry's sidebar and scene controls leave the screen, a GM's into two windows of the module's opened from a new upper row in the
corner; and the owner's decisions of 13.10 tidy the notice history. Most of it was measured in the headless harness, the screen's
layout also in Chromium on the glass harness, some only read in the code; none of it was tried in a real Foundry or at a table.

## Before installing

1. **Foundry's sidebar and scene controls are no longer on the screen.** A GM finds both in two windows of the module's: **Foundry
   tools** (the sidebar - the chat, the Scenes tab and the other directories) and **Map tools** (the scene controls). The new
   button with Foundry's logo, above the handbooks button, opens both and closes both. **The GM panel's button has moved:** it is
   the red button with the eye (a hexagon under Stained Glass) above the settings gear, no longer in the column under the clock. A
   player has no scene controls on the left any more (their sidebar was already hidden): a token is still selected and dragged as
   before and the module changes none of Foundry's keys, but drawing, map notes and the target button go with the bar (not tried
   on a real canvas: LIVE-E77-11).
2. **The way back.** The world setting **The module's windows for Foundry's sidebar and scene controls**, in the module's
   settings, is on by default. Off, after a reload, a GM's sidebar and scene controls stand where Foundry puts them, the module's
   panels leave room for them again and the Foundry tools button is not drawn; a player's screen is the same either way (read in
   the code and on the glass harness, not tried at a table: LIVE-E77-17).
3. **Room pictures.** Room Setup's Description tab has a new column, **Picture**: one picture per room, chosen with the picker or
   removed. Room Setup takes jpg (or jpeg), png, webp and avif from this server's files. It refuses svg, gif and every other type,
   a path to another site (S3 included), and a path with a query, a fragment or `..`; such a path is not saved and the GM is told:
   "{room}: the picture was not saved. Only a picture from this server's files can be used: jpg, png, webp or avif." An animated
   png, webp or avif saved under a still name is not detected and moves on every screen that shows the room (read in the code).
   The descriptions and pictures of all rooms reach every browser, as a scene's background does, so keep a room's secrets in its
   stashes and traces (the tab's note says so).
4. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back. **On The Forge, install from this
   release's manifest URL.**
5. **Settings, keys and texts.** Two new settings (125 registered, 123 at 1.2.75): the world switch above, and `foundryWindows`,
   hidden and per browser, where a GM last dropped the two windows. No new keybinding (Escape and Shift+C stay Foundry's, below);
   `game.drpg.toggleFoundryTools()` is new. `lang/en.json` goes from 3360 to 3374 strings (16 added, 2 removed, 6 reworded) and
   `lang/pl.json` from 4131 to 4145 (16 added, 2 removed, 5 reworded). For a GM, among others: the setting, the refused-picture
   warning above and the Description tab's new intro and note; the GM button's label is now "Open the GM panel". The handbooks
   were updated; the Foundry and Daggerheart versions in the manifest are unchanged.

## At the table

### The room tile

- **Where it stands.** Under Stained Glass on a computer (read in the code): under the clock, at the clock's width, when the clock
  leaves room for the tile's smallest box; otherwise right of the notice tile, clear of the history button's corner. On the glass
  harness in Chromium, for a GM and a player alike: under the clock at nine desk sizes (1400x900 to 3840x2160), beside the notices
  at seven (1224x768 to 1366x768, 1280x720 and 1366x657 included). Under Monokuma Legacy the same two places, as a flat panel that
  ends at least 16 px above the player list, or 16 px right of the notice stack; read under the clock at all sixteen desk sizes,
  beside the notices only where that place was forced (LIVE-E77-13).
- **What it shows.** Only the room your own character stands in, never another: its name, its search tokens, **Available project**
  when it holds a project you can work on, the GM's picture across the tile behind them, and the GM's description, which the
  chevron in the tile's corner (tooltip **Read more**, then **Show less**) unfolds over the picture and folds again; a new room
  folds it. Under Stained Glass the name and the project line are in capitals. Click the picture to see it large, on your screen
  alone (Foundry's own picture window: LIVE-E77-04); clicking a picture that does not load says "The picture of this room does not
  load." (read in the code). A GM's tile shows the room of the GM's own Monokuma, whatever token is selected; a GM without a
  Monokuma has an empty pane. During a Class Trial it shows no room. An Eclipse, a death or a Monocub does not hide the room.
- **When it changes.** Once a move is settled: a crossing still being judged, or refused and not yet put back, is not drawn, and
  in scenario 74 a refused crossing showed nothing of the refused room, 400 and 1200 ms after its last step too. On a co-owner's
  screen the tile follows a move about a second and a half late (1509 and 1516 ms headless), and a refusal put back more slowly
  than that would show the refused room for a moment; neither is tried at a table (LIVE-E77-15).
- **The clock** has no room lines: they are on the tile. Clicking the clock still explains where things stand, your room's
  description included; for a player it is now always about the same character as the clock and the tile (read in the code).
- **The move card** reads "You enter {room}." in English (was "Entered {room}.") and says what the crossing cost, without the
  room's description; cards already in the chat log keep theirs, styled as before (R2 reads the rule).
- **On a stacked screen** the tile is one row of the stack, 44 px high: a 78x44 picture (click it for the large one), the name,
  the tokens, **Available project**, and a **Description** button that opens the description in a window; a Class Trial or a GM
  without a Monokuma leaves no row (read in the code). The glass harness read the row at all seven stacked sizes, both themes and
  roles, and a GM's Foundry window opening over it (Chromium, stand-in sidebar; Foundry's own stacking is not measured). At
  1024x768 under Stained Glass the clock's column scrolls, and the last project's line is reached by scrolling (read by hand on
  the glass harness, not a line of the sweep).

### The GM's Foundry windows, the corner's upper row and a player's screen

- **The corner** has an upper row: the red GM button (a hexagon under Stained Glass) above the settings gear and the Foundry tools
  button above the book, both 44 px, every two neighbours 6 px apart. If Foundry's logo does not load (on a v14 table:
  LIVE-E77-09), the button shows a toolbox icon instead.
- **The windows** are dragged by their title bar and have no resize handle (read in the code). Each comes back where it was last
  dropped, on that browser; another browser keeps its own places. A window is kept wholly on the screen, 8 px in and clear of the
  corner's buttons, also when the browser window is resized or the window grows; a place remembered on a big screen comes back
  when the screen is big again. Never dragged, Foundry tools stands 420 px in from the right and 72 px down, and Map tools at 379,
  187 (the design's numbers for 1920x1080, not measured).
- **Escape** stays Foundry's: it cancels a drag on the canvas, closes Foundry's windows and menus and releases the selection as
  before; only when nothing of Foundry's is left does it close both windows. **Shift+C**, or anything that opens a sidebar tab,
  opens Foundry tools first. Closing Foundry tools collapses the sidebar, which is when Foundry shows its chat notifications (the
  design's reading of Foundry 14's code). All of this is read in the code, none of it tried at a table (LIVE-E77-10, LIVE-E77-06).
- **Under Monokuma Legacy** the text in the two windows wears the module's pixel face and the icons stay icons (measured on a
  stand-in sidebar, not Foundry's: LIVE-E77-18).
- **A player** has no scene controls and no sidebar. On every new canvas and every render of the controls the module puts a player
  back on the Tokens layer with its select tool, except from the Templates and Notes layers, which it leaves alone. What T, R, F
  and the ping do on a real canvas is not tried at a table yet (LIVE-E77-11, LIVE-E77-16).

### The notice history

- **Its foot** holds **Clear** alone, on the right; the line saying the history could not be saved appears only when that has
  happened. The paragraph on how long notices are kept (a player's and a GM's) is gone; the handbooks still give the limits.
- **Each entry shows its words once.** A card without a title takes its own heading as its title in the list, and its text no
  longer repeats that heading or the group's clock line.
- **Reworded:** an empty history says "No notices yet.", and Clear asks with "Every notice in this history goes, the cards about
  the murder too. They do not come back."
- **An Eclipse's group** is named for the time of day the Eclipse opens into, as its card is: over the card "Noon Eclipse", begun
  in the Morning, the group's heading now ends "NOON · ECLIPSE" (it ended "MORNING · ECLIPSE" in 1.2.75). One begun at Night names
  the next day's Morning and its session. A history kept before this release reads the same way; one Eclipse stays one group.

## Changed

- New files: `scripts/room-tile.mjs` (whose room, the tile, its stacked row and its window) and `scripts/foundry-windows.mjs` (the
  two windows, the launcher, the Tokens layer, Escape, the world switch). The picture is the region flag `drpgRoomImage`, read
  only through `vault.mjs` `safeRoomImage`. New hooks `drpgRouteSettled` (movement.mjs, once a route settles) and
  `drpgHudRendered`; `hudActor` is now `viewerActor` and the clock's `buildRoom` is gone. `relay-guard.mjs` and `module.json` are
  unchanged.
- New CSS tokens: `--drpg-room-*` (written by glass.mjs `roomPlacement`), `--drpg-tile-row-h`, `--drpg-launch-u-bottom`,
  `--drpg-roster-foot`. glass.mjs lost `GM_SLOT`, `GM_DROP`, `tightenGmGap`, `alignTo` and `RAIL_AT`, and gained `flatPlacement`
  for Monokuma Legacy. The notice history gained `rowWords`, `sayOnce` and `groupHeading`, and clock.mjs `clockAfter`, which
  `advanceTimeOfDay` now reads.
- The suite's own "tier 0/1 changed nothing" check now reads the module's client settings too, and tier 2 puts them back.
  The Foundry tools button falls back to its toolbox icon on every failed load of the logo, not only the first (r2-H6; R512).
- **New tests:** 19 numbered ones (5 in tier 0: R503, R506, R507, R509, R518; 14 in tier 1: R504, R505, R508, R510 to R517, R530
  to R532), 1 new tier-2 test ("Room Setup writes a room's picture"), and scenario 74-room-tile in the ci set (25, 24 at 1.2.75;
  it reads no cut of the glass, only the Chromium sweep does). R2, R107, R299, R379, R432, R472, R474 and R478 were changed (R379,
  R432 and R472 in their census rows); scenarios 66 and 73 too. The skip baseline goes from 18 to 22 rows (R508, R513, R514 and
  R515: a browser's layout or cascade). Next free: R533. `audit/glass-sweep.mjs` gained the room tile, the GM's windows, both
  roles, one size (1366x657) and a pinned place per size. In its runs at r2-H3 and on d2ba27b, opening and closing the two windows recut the glass
  0 times (21 GM lines with glass, a stand-in sidebar), and so did a new description or the description opened (74 lines).
- The notice history's group heading keeps each " ·" with the word before it (a no-break space), so a long heading wraps after a
  dot, never before one (r2-H8; scenario 73's H5 reads the text, as the headless harness draws no lines; a Chromium screenshot of
  the window at 1366x768 breaks it after a dot). The module's own accessibility and chrome passes no longer mark the inside of a
  kept card, and R294's window clause reads the entry the window shows after it redraws (r2-H9, after a checkpoint's R294 failure
  inside a Class Trial at 0dc9232).

## Known gaps

- Sixty live checks stand open (items 163 to 222 of the audit's section 9.2): the forty-two of 1.2.75 and LIVE-E77-01 to -18 - the
  P11 matrix (-01); Foundry's real windows (-02); the picture path on a real server (-03) and opened large (-04); typing through a
  resize (-05); chat notifications (-06); the state's colour (-07; only R515 reads it, and it skips headless); the owner's
  screenshots (-08); Foundry's answer on the logo, or plan B (-09); Escape and Shift+C beside other modules (-10); a player's keys
  (-11); saved places at 1366x768 (-12); Legacy and a real phone (-13); the picture under Foundry's windows (-14); a co-owner's
  1.5 s (-15); a template from a player's card (-16); the world switch (-17); Legacy's face in the windows (-18).
- Named from memory of earlier Foundry versions, not read on v14: `canvas.currentMouseManager`, which lets a drag be cancelled
  before Escape closes the windows (LIVE-E77-10), the Templates and Notes layer names (LIVE-E77-16), the call that returns a
  player to the Tokens layer (LIVE-E77-11), and the harness's ApplicationV2 `hasFrame`.
- The GM panel's clock line and the time of day's card still name a running Eclipse by the clock's own time ("Morning · ECLIPSE")
  while the clock and the history name the time it opens into (read in r2-H7, not changed).
- Not run in Foundry: R508, R513, R514 and R515 skip headless; R508's Legacy clause and R299's clause (c) never ran in a browser.
- Read in the code, not measured: a window taller than the screen is held by the stylesheet's height (700 px, or the screen less
  110 px when that is less), not by shrinking, and not measured with a v14 sidebar; whether Foundry re-renders a closed window;
  `%2f` and `%5c` refused without measuring Foundry's server; whether Foundry v14 reads a client setting from storage on every
  read, which the suite's put-back rests on. The picture layer's `will-change: transform` was measured in Chromium only; the
  stacked row's lazy picture and its order over the stack are not measured at a table.
- Under Monokuma Legacy the tile's name and project line are drawn as typed, not in capitals (no P11 picture for Legacy;
  LIVE-E77-08).
- The room tile is too large under Monokuma Legacy (430 x 491 px under the clock at 1920x1080 and at 1366x768 in the Chromium
  sweep) and under Stained Glass where it stands beside the notices (1366x768). The owner judged both on this release's
  screenshots; the next update makes them smaller. Stained Glass's tile under the clock stays as it is.
- Not in this release: the sentence about the world switch on the known-issues page (E82).
- A heading of the notice history can still wrap inside "Day 1" or "Session 1", where the spaces are ordinary (not measured).
- The checkpoint's R294 failure inside a Class Trial at 0dc9232 was not reproduced without forcing it: scenario 01 keeps 300
  characters of a failure, and the compared values were cut. r2-H9 changed what its probe showed could fail that clause (a redraw
  of the window, the accessibility pass, the chrome pass); that these caused the failure is not known. The run on d2ba27b below
  read the suite again once: scenario 01 20 of 20, R294 green inside the Class Trial.
